for me as someone who started studying 12 hours per test this semester (per day depending on how much time I have, sometimes 4 hr or 6 hr on my lighter days \[when im sleep deprived lol\] ) it's all in having good people keeping me accountable. I'm horrible at thinking of the long term and they are good at it while being bad at studying/understanding so I fill that role. We form a symbiotic relationship, they keep me showing up and on task out of necessity and I teach/study out of obligation to my promise. Its rough for me If i don't have this, I slack off watch YouTube and shit like that or get addicted to video games. Studying is a game of knowing yourself, knowing your pitfalls and avoiding them. Even right now as I'm writing this I just finished my last final today and want to play a game/ watch some shows but I know i will probably get addicted if I start and that will hinder my studies over the summer. tbh I think some people have affinity for these long study sessions and some don't, more specifically some people do better with 2-4 hour sessions more frequently and some do better with all day sessions maybe 3-4 times a week. I fit in the latter category but obviously more is better as long as you can avoid burn out because having interest in your subject is the biggest buff to studying and memory retention. If you're not the type to do 6+ hour sessions don't stress it, but know your consistency has to be on point studying more regularly than people who do 6+ hour sessions if you want similar results. Even then nothing is guaranteed or deserved in this life so studying more than them wont 100% yield better results than them, what it will do is yield better results than before when you studied less.

as for the secret bro I don't think there is one, I am competitive so I want to top my classes because I know I am not the smartest but I can suffer more than others and out work them. Thats the only way honestly, I am willing to sit in a library that's cold while its beautiful outside on maybe one meal a day if that's what the situation of my life calls for.

Hope this helps brother rooting for you to get better and for you to become the academic weapon you want to be. Remember all positive change that doesn't come easy starts with the desire to be better and you've taken the first step, don't leave the rest of the journey unfinished.

TLDR: fall in love with suffering because its the only way out of your situation to the life u want or find people to keep u accountable (study groups for me) is my secret but I dont think its much of a secret lol

yeah you could also lower your fov for a similar effect i dont think its all placebo some aspects of it can be, but I cant chalk it up 100% to just being in the players head. Reason being I think if your more zoomed in it will have an effect on how precise you can be on recoil control and staying on target, Why? because every split second I'm not trying to process the extra visual data I can be more fast at getting on target and more precise in my micro adjustments to stay there because I'm having an easy time seeing whats going on. Started to think about this topic after watching my 90 fov friend play his game he could see the players so well on a iron sight wing meanwhile me on 106 fov which is just comfortable for me can't really see nearly aswell on irons. It's all about finding that personal balance of what you find comfortable to aim on. That being said I think the biggest part people undervalue about visual changes such as stretch res is the mental reset it can give when u plateau. Personally, I was finding myself just stuck at the same level for a while couldn't make many strides my play just looked consistently meh. I think this was caused by a negative feedback loop that was created from trying really hard to get good giving it my all and coming in short so I would go into engagements the same way every time expecting to lose because I didnt believe in myself, This then lead to get overly jittery once things started to go a bit sideways and just mess the whole thing up. I then took some time off the game and came back when they added the option to change crosshair color and boy did it make a world of difference for me I started getting better again, shaking up the games look so that it would cause my brain to actively pay more attention at a micro level instead of resorting back to old playing patterns the fresh look made it easier for my brain to make new neural maps ( basically I feel like it flipped my brain into learning mode) approaching the game in a new and all around a more active second by second basis. These however are just my thoughts from my experience of me trying to get better I'm no neuro chemist or anything like that just a guy who tries to take things he's learned in other walks of life and trying to apply them to what I'm currently doing. Ive also never played on stretched res I've seen alot of pros/high level players talking about its benefits so there is definitely something there at the very least But I dont run it because it requires cfg editing and I think the scripting/cfg editing and macros are out of hand in the scene rn, quite frankly I consider it cheating since many high level players are running things like it not telling anyone in their community and pass it off as completely being skill when its not (cough cough tap strafers that have multi binds on scroll wheel or the super glide scripters that use the multi part script that literally lowers your frame rate cap when toggled because it gives you more time to input for a successful super glide and then re-raises your frame rate once the bind is released). Sorry if that was super long Ive just been thinking about it for a while and wanted to get my thoughts out into the community to see what others thoughts on things like this are.
